en.title: Minimum Road Reversals So Every City Reaches the Capital
en.description:
The underlying undirected graph is a tree, and each edge is currently one-way. Edges may be reversed so that every city can reach the capital, city 0. Find the minimum number of reversals.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N (2..50000), followed by N−1 lines a b, each meaning a→b; 0≤a,b<N, a≠b, and the underlying graph is guaranteed to be a tree.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: 0→1, 1→3, and 4→5 must be reversed, for 3 in total. Example 2: 1→2 and 3→4 must be reversed, for 2 in total. Example 3: every edge already points toward 0, so 0 reversals.
hints: Traverse the undirected tree from 0. If a parent–child edge originally points from parent to child, it must be reversed; if it points from child to parent, keep it. Count the edges of the first kind.
